note: .env.example not read (permission denied). Return tool has a real approve/decline step and runs only after the customer approves.

labels.what: Demo data for a store called Northwind Gear: orders, products with stock, shipments and help articles in module arrays; header says real deployment would call the shop database, carrier API and CRM
lookup_order reads the hardcoded orders array
track_shipment reads hardcoded shipments and simulates a flaky carrier with sleep (4000 ms for a -SLOW tracking number)
check_stock reads the hardcoded products array
Approved return returns a made-up return id and a label_url on returns.example.com; no return is created in any system
book_callback adds the slot to an in-memory Set and returns a booking id; nobody is notified and the booking is lost on restart
book_callback books straight from the model call, with no customer approval step (create_return_request has one)
book_callback has date, slot, phone-format and topic length checks but no per-session limit on bookings; a loop can fill every slot
RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 30 and CARD_RETURN_SHIPPING = 6.95 hardcoded; they are enforced in code, not only in prompt
Fixed today date 2026-09-25 so return windows are deterministic; the real date is never used unless DEMO_TODAY is unset elsewhere
localhost log URL; port default 3000 in config.ts line 13
No user login; the client-chosen sessionId is the only identity. /api/chat, /api/confirm and /api/reset are open and no rate limit, so anyone can spend the model key
Any order can be looked up by number alone (no customer identity check); email is masked but names, items and tracking are returned
Sessions held in a process Map with no expiry, so memory grows with each new sessionId
